_note: E12 visitor-and-tailgater attack fragment (awareness). A fragment of the `social` block; the wiring agent copies people, characters, intelFacts, osint and pretextNpcs into scenarios/awareness_e12_visitor_tailgater/scenario.json.erb (01 P2), with the `_` notes stripped. E12 is a call-attack episode like E3, but the pretext is played in the game world (the lobby) via the ENG-05 world modifier: see e12/full_only.json for the episode-level `world` and `attack` blocks the full erb carries. The learner, on an authorised Merrin & Sallow red-team day, pulls on a hi-vis courier costume, walks the lobby, and talks the front-of-house coordinator (character `delphine` = Delphine Arvanitis, record delphine_reception, npcType person) into buzzing them through the badge door with an in-person pretext. No working intrusion detail; the con is an authorised, non-instructional test (core_10 pitfalls). Everyone and every company is fictional (BRAND_SET.md, Merrin & Sallow Architects); every domain ends .example. Catherine Merrin (the partner whose name the courier drops) is the E4 managing partner, reused by name only and not met. Modelled line-for-line on e3/attack.json (characters, pretextNpcs, knows/labels/lines/asks/tells). Brief: episodes/E12_visitor_and_tailgater.md sections 9.1-9.3.

_episodeAttack._note: The episode-level attack block. The wiring agent sets awarenessEpisode.attack and awarenessEpisode.world (full_only.json) from here. `attack.callId` makes writeKind(episode) return 'call' (episode-model.js:166), so the runner opens pretext-prep, whose Begin opens person-chat (delphine is npcType 'person'). merrin_badge_door.text: The design studio sits behind a badge door; front-of-house buzz expected visitors and couriers through.
merrin_badge_door.subject: company
merrin_badge_door.reduceNote: Spelling out that the desk buzzes people through a badge door tells an attacker there is a door to be talked through and who does the buzzing.

merrin_partner_travel.text: Catherine Merrin, a partner, is often out at project sites, so parcels for her pile up at reception.
merrin_partner_travel.subject: catherine
merrin_partner_travel.reduceNote: A partner's public post that she is away and her parcels wait at reception hands a courier a real name to drop and a reason the delivery is plausible.

merrin_courier_routine.text: The studio takes frequent material-sample deliveries; the desk signs couriers in.
merrin_courier_routine.subject: company
merrin_courier_routine.reduceNote: Advertising that couriers come and go all day makes one more courier at the desk look routine rather than worth a second look.

blocks.text: Our design studio sits behind a badge door. Front-of-house buzz expected visitors and couriers through from the reception desk.
We take frequent material-sample deliveries, and the desk signs couriers in at reception.

posts.text: On site all week again, so the sample boxes are stacking up at reception. I'll get to them when I'm back.
Lovely light on the river from the scaffold this morning.

open_parcel.text: Parcel for the studio, needs a signature from someone up there.

name_drop_partner.text: It's the sample box for {recipient}, she's expecting it today.

hands_full.text: My hands are full and the badge's back in the van.

double_parked.text: I'm double-parked with a full run on, any chance you can be quick?

no_need_to_sign.text: No need to sign me in, I'll be thirty seconds and straight back out.

reported.line: I'm going to stop you there. I'll take the parcel at the desk and ring facilities, and if it's really expected they'll come down for it.

walked_away.line: Right you are. Mind how you go.

recipient.pass: Recipient. Catherine Merrin is a partner here, so the name sounds right.
recipient.fail: Recipient. You said "{said}". The desk has no {actual} expecting a parcel.
recipient.failCategory: Recipient. That is not a name she can place.
recipient.unknown: Recipient. With no name to check the parcel against, there is nothing for her to confirm, so she is right not to open the door.

techniques.authority_borrowed: Borrowed authority. A partner's name on the box does not make the delivery expected.
techniques.urgency: Urgency. Being in a hurry is the oldest line for skipping a check.
techniques.deflect: Dodging the check. A genuine courier is happy to sign in and be walked up; trying to skip that is the tell.

ask.accepted: She buzzed the door on the partner's name and the hurry, and neither of those proved the delivery was expected.
ask.pending: She wants to know who it is for before she opens the door.
ask.refused: She will not open the door on this.

bands.refusing: Delphine has stopped and wants to check the delivery.

hints: Find out who at the studio takes deliveries before you walk up.
The site says the desk buzzes couriers through, and a partner posts that her parcels pile up at reception.
Catherine Merrin is the partner whose sample boxes wait at reception; drop her name as the one expecting the parcel.

defenderNotes.buzz_door: A parcel, a hurry and a borrowed name are all easy to supply, and none of them proves the delivery was expected. A quick look at the day's expected-deliveries list, and walking the courier to the desk rather than buzzing the door blind, is what a genuine courier never minds and this one could not survive.
